plan_ref: planning/steward-chamber-2026-08-09/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md :: Wave 3 (C10 - F6 both-tree living routes inventory)
law: Every EXISTING Anchor state-changing (POST) handler AND every Ecgberht bridge verb (seal-chamber-bridge.mjs modes, commission-run-bridge.mjs verbs) carries a row here. The CI diff guard (chamber_enforcement.diff_inventory_vs_code, exercised by tests/test_chamber_routes_inventory_w3.py) fails when a route or verb exists in code without an inventory row, AND when a row goes stale - a living registry, never a Phase-0 snapshot. Every row is proven RED-TO-GREEN (its F6 assertion set shown FAILING on an auth-off server, then green auth-on) by tests/test_chamber_red_to_green_w3.py. New mutators landed by W8-W11 add their row + red-to-green proof in their landing wave.
sibling_resolution: Ecgberht verb rows resolve against the sibling repo root: env ECGBERHT_ROOT when set, else <anchor-root>/../Ecgberht (same law as scripts/run-all-tests.mjs). Never an absolute host path.
scope_note: Bridge scope is exactly the plan's: seal-chamber-bridge.mjs modes + commission-run-bridge.mjs verbs. Other Ecgberht scripts (high-seat-bridge.mjs, chamber-ui-bridge.mjs) are reached only through Anchor routes already carried as anchor_routes rows; if a later wave gives them their own verb surface, their rows land with that wave. GET routes are read surfaces (read-only by the route-table law) and are outside the state-changing inventory by definition.

browser.caller: A browser page (the dashboard, or any hostile page a browser user visits). The hostile case is a CSRF-class forged cross-origin request: hostile Origin/Referer, a no-preflight content type, the victim's HttpOnly auth cookie riding along automatically.
required: token: every state-changing POST requires the shared-secret token (X-Anchor-Token header / Authorization / JSON-body token) when ANCHOR_TOKEN is configured - 401 before any handler substance
post-only: the mutator is not invocable via GET (a GET twin may serve a read surface, never the mutation)

csrf-refusal: a forged cross-origin request carrying the auth COOKIE but (being cross-site) no token header is refused 401 - the explicit token header is the CSRF defense; SameSite on the cookie is a browser courtesy the server never depends on

bridge-cli.caller: A non-browser caller of the HTTP surface: a bridge script, a CLI, curl, or a forged agent process (no Origin/Referer, arbitrary User-Agent). The Ecgberht bridge processes themselves are host-local child processes spawned by already-authenticated Anchor handlers (payload over stdin, never a network listener) - their NETWORK exposure is exactly the anchor_routes rows listed in each verb's exposed_via.
required: token: the auth token is still required - the non-browser class is asserted NON-exempt; a forged non-browser caller cannot skip the checks
no-exemption: there is no header, user-agent, or origin-absence that bypasses the token gate

coverage_rule.rule: Every new-surface test file in the namespace MUST carry an AUTH-ON tag in its header: 'AUTH-ON: enforced' (the file exercises HTTP surfaces with ANCHOR_TOKEN set - a real authenticated session via the scripted-login fixture) or 'AUTH-ON: not-a-surface' (the file exercises no HTTP surface and must not boot or probe a server). The scanner (chamber_enforcement.scan_new_surface_tests, run in CI by tests/test_chamber_routes_inventory_w3.py) fails the suite naming any untagged or dishonestly-tagged file. Chamber waves W6-W11 land their surface tests in this namespace so the rule binds them mechanically.
coverage_rule.why: The chamber shipped broken twice because virtually every test ran auth-off; a green tokenless suite sat on top of a broken authed dashboard. The tag makes the auth posture of every new-surface test an asserted, scanned property instead of a hope.

red_to_green.proof: tests/test_chamber_red_to_green_w3.py boots a hermetic auth-OFF server and shows, for EVERY row below, the F6 token assertion FAILING (the tokenless probe reaches dispatch); then boots an auth-ON server and shows the full F6 set green for every row. The dispatch shim used sits AFTER the real do_POST auth middleware, so the auth path exercised is the production path on a real socket; no mutating handler body ever executes.
red_to_green.auth_off_condition: ANCHOR_TOKEN unset (and ANCHOR_AUTH_MODE not 'enforce') - the exact condition under which the chamber shipped broken twice.
